Exempt the proxy from battery optimization

A restart after a reboot needs two gates: this app exempt from battery optimization, and enabled in DokeOS Auto Start Management (System Manager → App Management → Auto Start Management). This asks for the battery one. Without both, the tile still works, but the proxy does not come back after a reboot.

Auto Start Management: unreadable — the DokeOS list is protected by com.freeme.freemanager.permission.ACCESS_INTERFACE, so the app cannot read it. Check System Manager → App Management → Auto Start Management, or run wireless-adb-keeper/autostart-allow.sh \"Phone link proxy\" / phone-link-tools/autotoggle.

Auto Start Management: likely blocked this boot (noticed %1$s) — no boot broadcast reached the app. Enable \"Phone link proxy\" in System Manager → App Management → Auto Start Management, or run wireless-adb-keeper/autostart-allow.sh \"Phone link proxy\" / phone-link-tools/autotoggle. This is a suspicion; the vendor list cannot be read.
The TCP port this proxy listens on. 1080 is the SOCKS convention; two running proxies need two ports. The laptop points at this port on the phone\'s address.

How many SOCKS connections this proxy may have open at once: 16 to 1024, 256 by default. Each live connection costs two threads, so a higher ceiling spends memory and CPU. Raise it when a desktop browser fills the listener and requests start failing. The selector-based relay that removes the thread cost is tracked separately (#37).
The SOCKS5 user name the laptop sends. It is stored with this proxy and never shown in dumpsys or the log; the password is the only secret.
The SOCKS5 password. It lives in the app\'s private preferences, is never printed by dumpsys or the log, and is dropped entirely when the proxy listens without authentication.
The only Wi-Fi the port opens on. On this network the listener serves; on another the service stays up with the port closed and opens again when the phone comes back.
Open the port on whatever network the phone is on. Simpler, but the phone then offers the proxy on every Wi-Fi it joins — the credentials still apply.
Accept clients without a user and password. Anyone who can reach the port can then relay through the phone, so only on a network you trust.

Come back by itself: at boot, and whenever the phone joins the SSID. A reboot start needs two gates: the battery exemption (the line under the switch reports it) and DokeOS Auto Start Management (System Manager → App Management → Auto Start Management). The second cannot be read from the app, so a clear battery line alone does not promise a restart.

The Quick Settings tile is one switch, and this binds this proxy to it. While anything is bound the tile starts them all and stops them all, and a proxy that is not bound is left as it is; with nothing bound it starts the proxy in use, and its click stops everything. The line under the switch says what the tile does now.

Switch Android\'s wireless debugging back on when the phone joins the SSID, so adb can still reach it after a reboot. That needs WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, which phone-proxy-install grants; without it the app says so instead of failing silently.

Ask Android to keep the Wi-Fi association while a Wi-Fi listener is bound, instead of leaving an access point that has no internet. This is an experiment: Android 14+ treats the lock as low latency, and may only honour that with the screen on and the app in the foreground. It costs battery while held, and a paused listener or one started with any_network does not hold it.
Store the form in this proxy without starting or stopping anything. Start saves first as well, so Save is for keeping a change you are not ready to run.
Throw the unsaved edits away and show what the store holds for this proxy.

Start this proxy with the settings on these pages — the form is stored first — or stop it. Start adds a listener: the proxies already running keep listening, unless one of them holds this port, which this one then takes over. Starting also marks this proxy in use, the mark on its card — that is the proxy the Quick Settings tile and a restart after a reboot start. Stop stops this proxy alone; the service goes away with the last listener.
Another proxy: it copies this one\'s credentials and network and takes the next free port, then opens for its own settings.

The last 200 things that happened to this proxy, newest first, plus the bytes this run moved and a sparkline of the last minute. It lives in memory; `adb logcat -s phone-link-proxy` keeps the full record.
Start or stop from the list

Start this proxy with its saved settings without opening it, or stop it while it is running. Both are about this proxy alone: the others keep listening, and Start marks it in use, which is what the tile starts.
Open the app to start the proxy
